text:
liz: Customer reports duplicate final completions after a short network drop. They saw two final messages for the same prompt and were billed twice. session=abc123, resume_token=rTkn-9, request_id in their logs: req-77-zz. Happened around 2026-08-11 14:02 UTC. Please advise next steps and whether billing hold is possible.

tariq: Thanks — can you paste a minimal repro and the exact client logs? Did the client include an idempotency key on the original stream request or on reconnect?

liz: Repro steps from customer: 1) open SSE stream to /v1/streams with session=abc123 2) simulate flaky mobile network (drop for ~2s) 3) SDK auto-reconnects and sends resume_token=rTkn-9 4) client receives the remaining chunks and then also gets an extra final completion chunk (so two finals).
They attached a short SDK snippet:```js
// mobile sdk pseudocode
fetch('/v1/streams', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer x', 'Idempotency-Key': 'ik-123' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'rwd-mini', prompt: 'summarize', session: 'abc123', resume_token: 'rTkn-9' })
})
```
But customer said their SDK v0.9.1 didn't surface the Idempotency-Key on reconnect path, so the reconnect request came without the header.

hao: I pulled server-side logs for req-77-zz. We see two completion events emitted ~800ms apart: gen_id=gen-1 (emitted before disconnect), gen_id=gen-2 (emitted after reconnect). Both reference session abc123 and final_token_offset identical. The early partials were replayed on resume then gen-2 produced a finalization because the resumed worker thought it needed to finish generation. Looks like a race where resume landed on a replica that didn't have the warm KV state so it started a fresh finalization instead of attaching to the in-progress generator.

kelsey: Customer is asking for a refund for the duplicate charge. Can we put the charge on hold while we investigate? @billing-team please advise.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-789 linked to streaming resume duplication. Severity: P2.

dave: Short-term mitigation we can recommend to customers: 1) ensure client preserves and sends Idempotency-Key on reconnect requests, 2) upgrade to SDK >= v0.9.3 (we've patched the reconnect header propagation there), or 3) set reconnect=false and retry with backoff to avoid automatic resume. For internal engineering: repro steps I used: run a local proxy that drops TCP for 100-2000ms, reproduce with curl -N and an explicit Idempotency-Key to validate dedupe.

liz: Important note from customer: their mobile SDK did NOT forward the original Idempotency-Key on the automatic reconnect request. That explains the server treating the resumed request as a new generation.

tariq: Filed runtime ticket RT-456 describing the race. Proposed fixes: - ensure reconnect keeps original headers (idempotency, trace ids) - on resume, server should check for an active generation with same session+prompt prefix and prefer attach-over-start if prefix matches - add 10s duplicate-finalization dedupe window so finalization emits are deduped by session+offset.

kelsey: Billing team acknowledged and will hold the duplicate charge pending confirmation of duplicate emission. I'll keep customer informed and promise a refund if we confirm.

hao: Deployed a canary mitigation: when resume_token present, server attempts to fetch original idempotency header from session metadata and will skip spawning a new generator if it finds a matching in-progress generation. Monitoring for duplicate finals enabled.

liz: Customer tested workaround (upgrade to v0.9.3) and confirmed they no longer see double finals. They accepted the temporary refund hold and asked for timeline for permanent fix. They also provided device logs showing reconnect path lacked headers which matched our hypothesis. :white_check_mark:

Notes/actions: RT-456 created, INC-2026-789 incident, follow-up: add unit test for resume attach logic, postmortem to document race and customer impact, confirm billing refund after server dedupe verification.
